clue.text: General disapproval except at the curtain of Dick Whittington

definitions.text: General disapproval except at the curtain of Dick Whittington

parts.words: General disapproval except at the curtain of Dick Whittington
parts.note: jeering shouts from an audience show displeasure, except in the pantomime, where the hero's feline companion takes its bow at the final curtain

explanation.surface: An audience boos everyone except when the curtain falls on the Christmas pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington is a classic British Christmas pantomime whose hero has a famous cat; at the curtain the cat 'calls' (takes its bow), while elsewhere the word means jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrill whistles and jeers are the noise a disapproving crowd makes.

clue.text: A Silk " seen about a case

definitions.text: A Silk " seen about a case

parts.words: A Silk " seen about a case
parts.note: a senior barrister is a 'silk' who takes a case, but here silk wraps around a case of the pupa

explanation.surface: A Queen's Counsel is seen working on a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister is called a Silk; the stray mark is from the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: A silkworm spins a protective silken casing around itself before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Fold towards the middle, possibly to count sheep

definitions.meaning: to go to bed, where the sleepless count sheep

explanation.surface: A shepherd folds his flock in, perhaps to count them.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges are bent inward, and the informal phrase means going to bed.

clue.text: By no means down on one's uppers

definitions.text: By no means down on one's uppers

parts.words: By no means down on one's uppers
parts.note: being on one's uppers is British slang for being broke; the opposite, rising high, is suggested

explanation.surface: Not at all short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: On one's uppers means penniless, worn down to the shoe uppers; the answer means rising, in the upper position.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising in power or influence, the very opposite of being in decline.

clue.text: It's profitless, as Shakespeare's lost play

definitions.text: It's profitless, as Shakespeare's lost play

parts.words: It's profitless, as Shakespeare's lost play
parts.note: work done for no pay, echoing the title of a Shakespeare comedy in which effort is wasted

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare play that made no money and has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: The comedy Love's Labour's Lost is not a lost play; 'lost' is borrowed from its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Work undertaken for pleasure rather than payment earns nothing.

clue.text: Joan's spasm of cold

parts.note: Joan of Arc, the French saint, gives her surname
a tic is an involuntary muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Joan suffers a shivering fit from the chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar regions are bitterly cold, so the adjective names freezing weather.

clue.text: A gathering of the Lacey's, say?

definitions.text: A gathering of the Lacey's, say?

parts.words: A gathering of the Lacey's, say?
parts.note: looks like a family reunion, but describes a frill of gathered lace

explanation.surface: A family reunion of the Laceys.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill of pleated or gathered fabric trims dresses.

clue.text: Not only traders and unions do so to speak

definitions.text: Not only traders and unions do so to speak

parts.words: Not only traders and unions do so to speak
parts.note: shopkeepers and trade unionists discuss business, but any idle discussion forum is called this

explanation.surface: Merchants and unions are not alone in negotiating.
explanation.walkthrough: Traders deal in shops and unions organise shop floors, so 'talking shop' fits them literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum for endless discussion without action, or chatting about work.

clue.text: She does not run a teahouse

definitions.text: She does not run a teahouse

parts.words: She does not run a teahouse
parts.note: char is slang for tea, but this woman cleans houses

explanation.surface: A woman who is not the proprietor of a café.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'char' is tea; a char or charlady is a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaner employed to do housework.

clue.text: Smoking steeds that show their oats?

definitions.text: Smoking steeds that show their oats?

parts.words: Smoking steeds that show their oats?
parts.note: cobs are sturdy horses, and corn is grain such as oats; the smoking ones are pipes made from maize husks

explanation.surface: Horses with steam rising from them display the grain they have eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a short, stocky riding horse, and in Britain 'corn' can mean any cereal crop, oats included; the pipes are made from maize.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco pipes carved from dried maize ears are what smokers puff on here.

clue.text: To wit, friend turns monstrous

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'namely' or 'to wit'

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for friend is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Namely, a companion becomes a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches an adjective to point at the six-headed monster of the Strait of Messina.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this creature was a six-headed sea monster facing Charybdis.

clue.text: What the defence is doing prestigiously

definitions.meaning: read as two words, possessing standing or status

explanation.surface: A defence counsel performing impressively.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenders resist attack, and with standing means having status.

clue.text: Tear-jerker, one included in Marmion's last words

indicators.note: included in signals that the numeral is placed inside the dying words

parts.note: in Scott's poem Marmion the dying hero cries 'On, Stanley, on!', so the outer words are on ... on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weepy story about one character in Scott's poem and his dying cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmion is Walter Scott's narrative poem; its hero's famous last words are 'Charge, Chester, charge! On, Stanley, on!'
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this bulb vegetable makes the eyes water, so it literally jerks tears.

clue.text: A joint for angling rods for all

definitions.meaning: a coupling that lets two shafts meet at an angle, as in a car's drive shaft

explanation.surface: A fishing-rod connector suitable for everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cardan-type coupling connects rods set at angles, and the adjective means applicable to everyone.

clue.text: Singularly reliable lexicographer?

parts.note: a dictionary compiler deals in vocabulary, but keeping to a single promise marks a trustworthy person

explanation.surface: A dictionary writer who is uniquely dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' is the trick: a lexicographer is a man of words, plural; one of his word, singular, keeps promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps promises is called trustworthy in this idiom, playing on vocabulary.

clue.text: Drown in the Sound

parts.note: looks like sinking in a sea channel, but means silencing a speaker with noise

explanation.surface: Sink into the sea strait.
explanation.definitionFit: To silence someone by yelling over them.

clue.text: Does Flora itch to grow it?

definitions.text: Does Flora itch to grow it?

parts.words: Does Flora itch to grow it?
parts.note: the name of this wild flower was once thought to cure the itch of scabies

explanation.surface: Is the gardener eager to grow it?
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with pincushion flowers, formerly used against skin complaints.

clue.text: Rode ship shape' not quite round this globe

indicators.note: shape here works as a verb, the letters are given a new form

explanation.surface: Sailed a ship around a world that is not quite circular.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earth is not a perfect sphere but slightly flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-sphere, like the slightly flattened Earth.

clue.text: Re this submission for another going-over

indicators.note: this plus the two letters stands for the longer word, so they are taken off it to leave the solution

parts.note: a recapitulation is a summary going over the points again
taken as written

explanation.surface: Regarding this surrender, a further inspection is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' means the answer: put RE in front of it and you get RECAPITULATION, a going-over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender on agreed terms is a formal yielding to the enemy.

clue.text: Parent and I get round legality in Africa

indicators.note: get round signals the two parts surround the word for legality

parts.note: ma is a mother, a parent
law is legality

explanation.surface: A mother and I find a way around the law in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: The tiller's herd?

parts.note: a farmer's cattle, but also the action of a boat's tiller

explanation.surface: The farmer's cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Young bullocks, and what a helmsman's tiller does.

clue.text: Busybody, though venerable, frequently played

parts.note: a busy bee is a proverbial busy creature
tho' is an informal spelling of though
Ven. abbreviates Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A meddler, despite being elderly and respected, often joins in games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequently played' looks like describing the busybody, but it defines a composer whose music is often performed.
explanation.definitionFit: The German composer's symphonies are among the most often performed pieces in concert halls.

clue.text: Could be of the sea shore perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be rearranged differently

explanation.surface: Might be belonging to the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A seahorse is a fish named after a steed.

clue.text: Lovely lady popping up

definitions.meaning: a beautiful woman whose health is drunk, the belle of the town
bread browned in a pop-up machine jumps out when done

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman suddenly appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated beauty was the person drunk to at dinner, and grilled bread springs from the machine.

clue.text: Effluvia in mixing sour dough (no disgusted comment)

indicators.note: mixing tells us the remaining letters of the bread are stirred into a new order
no means the exclamation is left out of the bread letters

parts.note: taken as written
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Smells rise as someone kneads tangy bread without complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes UGH out of SOURDOUGH, leaving SOURDO; 'mixing' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant exhalations or emanations are smells given off.

clue.text: Bismarck, when dropped, how old?

parts.note: Tenniel's 1890 Punch cartoon 'Dropping the Pilot' showed the chancellor dismissed; the question about age supplies the rest

explanation.surface: How old was the German chancellor when he was dismissed?
explanation.walkthrough: Bismarck was famously drawn as a ship's pilot leaving the vessel; PILOT plus AGE (how old?) gives the guiding of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiding a ship through difficult waters is the work of a qualified navigator.

clue.text: Somewhat more than damp is a turf retreat

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A hideaway made of turf is rather wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through, waterlogged, wetter than merely damp.

clue.text: Siege can generate natural forces

indicators.note: generate implies producing something new, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A siege can produce powers of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents or means through which nature acts are forces at work.
